messages:
Priya Patel: Quick follow-up thread from today's all-hands for the engineering-process Q&A (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). Drop short questions and we'll answer in the live follow-up + post notes.

Zoe Kim: Are we keeping weekly trains for hosted or switching to a safer 2-week cadence? Ops team felt churn lately.

Priya Patel: Weekly remain the baseline for hosted to keep rapid iteration. We will formalize a predictable set of exception windows: infra-migration weeks, major DB migrations, and security hotfix weeks can opt into a scheduled 2-week freeze. Those exceptions must be announced 7d prior and approved by Eng Ops.

Diego Ramos: For weekly trains, what are the precise canary staging steps? any per-route throttles?

Priya Patel: Canary steps: (1) deploy to 5% of traffic for 30m, (2) expand to 25% for 60m if stable, (3) full rollout. Per-route throttles: route-specific traffic caps exist for high-fanout routes (config in Releases). Canary abort if any of: error-rate delta >0.5% absolute, p95 latency +20% vs baseline, or new dependency error spikes.

Samir Gupta: Do we require the full perf suite before merge for runtime-impacting changes, or is smoke OK? Also where do people add the perf label?

Priya Patel: For runtime-impacting changes: smoke perf checks + unit tests required pre-merge. Full perf suite runs in the post-merge promotion pipeline; if it flags regressions, the change is blocked from broad pools until mitigated. Add the label "perf-smoke" in PR descriptions to trigger specialized runners. We'll add a PR template snippet.

Zoe Kim: Oncall rotation: several ICs requested 2-week rotations for SRE. Any timeline?

Priya Patel: We're piloting 2-week rotations for SRE/infra starting next sprint across two teams. Runtime product oncall will stay 1-week due to current headcount. Oncall changes include: paid handover overlap (30m), documented incident handoff checklist, and a new swap policy (1x free swap per quarter).

Diego Ramos: How are SLAs calculated for Dedicated customers? do we pro-rate credits for partial outages?

Priya Patel: SLA tiers: hosted public = 99.9 target; Dedicated customers can contract 99.95 for reserved pools. Credits are pro-rated based on uptime windows per contract terms; we'll publish a sample SLA calc doc with examples (e.g., 8h downtime on a 30-day month = X% reduction). Legal is finalizing wording but we'll publish the matrix next week.

Samir Gupta: Quality bars: are we going to enforce a repo-level coverage minimum? some shared libs are light on tests.

Priya Patel: No single blanket number. Expect minimum: CI green + unit tests for new logic + integration tests for surfaced behaviors. Recommendations: libraries >=60%, runtime & customer-facing services >=80%. We'll add a repo-level README indicating expected quality bar and a short checklist in new PR templates (lint, typecheck, unit, perf-smoke if applicable).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for train/2026-05-04 (build: 2026.05.04-ff12).

Zoe Kim: Will the console expose canary health per route (p50/p95/error-rate) or only service-level?

Priya Patel: Console: yes — per-route p50/p95 + error-rate + a historical mini-chart in the Releases view. We'll also add a "canary-health" badge (green/yellow/red) and an explanation tooltip for thresholds. Alex from UX will share mocks in the follow-up doc.

Diego Ramos: Any immediate action items from this thread? owners?

Priya Patel: Action items: (1) I'll produce a 1-page FAQ and exception policy (owner: Priya) by EOD Fri. (2) Diego to draft the canary routing policy doc (owner: Diego) — please include route caps. (3) Samir to sketch PR template updates with perf-smoke label (owner: Samir). We'll post these to #eng-docs and iterate.

Zoe Kim: Thanks — will upvote the rota pilot.

Priya Patel: Thanks all — live Q&A in 25m and we'll post the recording + notes after. :thumbsup:
